newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan takes Indonesia car issue to WTO.
newsitem.headline: Japan takes Indonesia car issue to WTO.

text.p: Japan said on Friday that it has formally complained to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Indonesia's plan to build a domestic automobile.

"Japan has requested the Indonesian government to hold consultation on its car policy," based on the world trade rules set in 1994, the Foreign and Trade ministries said in a joint statement. They said the complaint was filed with the world trade body in Geneva on Friday.

Trade Ministry officials said earlier this week that Japan would take the complaints to the world trade body, forming a united front with its traditional trade adversary, the United States, as well as the European Union.
Indonesia said in February that a firm controlled by President Suharto's youngest son would get tax breaks to make sedans in collaboration with South Korea's Kia Motors.

Earlier on Friday, Trade Minister Shunpei Tsukahara told reporters that Japan had decided to make the complaint to the world trade body after asking Indonesia three times to make the national car plan conform with international trade rules. He added that both countries wanted to keep the trade dispute from harming friendly ties.
Japanese makers have a 95 percent share of the Indonesian vehicle market through joint-venture assembly and licensing arrangements with local firms and view the national car project as a threat.
As well as the joint ventures, Japan also exported 36,000 cars worth about $247 million to Indonesia in 1995.
But Tokyo -- the biggest aid donor country to Indonesia -- has ruled out using trade or aid as retaliatory steps to press Jakarta for a quick solution.

On Tuesday, Washington warned that Indonesia's policies of granting tax and tariff benefits to "national car" makers based on the percentage of domestic content in their vehicles would also be subject to a U.S. complaint to the WTO.
This was followed by announcement on Thursday by the European Union that it had decided to launch a formal complaint with the WTO on Indonesia's car policy.
